name: Fusion Finance Ltd
title: Fusion Finance Ltd - 543652 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Fusion Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR62 crore (ROA near 3%) as GNPA fell to 2.51% from 3.21% and credit cost eased to INR40 crore.
summary.overview: Disbursements grew 88% YoY to INR1,783 crore and AUM rose about 4% QoQ to INR7,702 crore, with collection efficiency above 99.75%. Reported PAT was INR62 crore and PBT rose about 67% QoQ to INR62.4 crore, with no management overlay release this quarter after a INR10 crore release last quarter. NIM expanded to 11.93% (up about 160 bps YoY and 49 bps QoQ), and marginal cost of borrowing fell to 10.1%. Management reiterated the INR10,000 crore AUM target for FY27 and flagged liquidity normalisation and a capital raise in roughly 1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: +67% QoQ from INR37 crore in Q4 FY26
from INR56 crore in Q4 FY26; seventh straight quarterly decline
vs INR87 crore in Q1 FY26
from 12.6% in Q1 FY26 (about -250 bps); from 10.3% in Q4 FY26
normalised ~10.3% excluding INR4 crore MTM (Q4 FY26: 10.4%)
targeted to fall to about INR1,400-1,450 crore by end Q2
PBT expected to equal PAT for about 24-26 months

segments.name: MFI
segments.commentary: Core book; PQM model covers about 250 branches. Fusion+2 guardrail relaxed in about 80% of category A branches, with the new-to-Fusion share rising to about 37% in Q1, near 39% in June and 42% in July. Individual loan launch targeted for early September; pricing roughly the same or up to 100 bps lower.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book about INR800 crore, disbursing about INR50 crore a month at INR7.5-8 lakh average ticket; collection efficiency above 99.25-99.3%. Plan to scale to 15% of the mix next year and 20% in two years, using about 200 MFI branches as hub-and-spoke and entering Tamil Nadu.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of INR10,000 crore for FY27 retained, implying roughly 44-45% of disbursements in H1 and 55% in H2; longer-term growth framed as 20-25% CAGR.
NIM expected to rise a further 15-20 bps by year-end (management says up to 25 bps), assuming no rate cuts; 55 bps of customer yield hikes only 12 bps reflected in the book so far.
Credit cost seen nearer 2% than 3% annualised based on the first four to four-and-a-half months; prior guidance of about 2.5% overall retained.
Net branch count to fall by about 40-50 (about 100 closures and 50-60 openings by Q3); branch network capped around 1,350-1,400 for INR12,000 crore AUM.
Opex to rise 4-5% in FY27 per AOP before a 2-3% saving from rationalisation; opex/average AUM to reach about 6-7% over time.
Capital raise to be initiated about 6-7 months before need; no raise needed for roughly 1.5 years (to mid-FY28); internal floor for Tier 1 of 23-25% versus 15% regulatory minimum.
capex_capacity: Plan to open about 50-60 new MFI branches and close about 100 by Q3 FY27, a net reduction of about 40-50 branches.
Around 50 of 200 identified MFI branches in MSME catchments are being taken up immediately for MSME sourcing (hub-and-spoke model).

Individual loan product Board-approved; system development underway, first loan targeted by first week of September 2026; average ticket around INR1.5 lakh and individual loans expected to be about 10% of MFI disbursements over time.
Fusion is registering under the borrower credit guarantee scheme, piloting in 2-3 markets from end of the quarter; less than 5% of book expected.

Liquidity: INR1,880 crore on balance sheet, about INR2,300 crore undrawn sanctions and about INR2,000 crore funding pipeline. CGS (MFI 2) sanctions of about INR480 crore received, with INR520 crore in pipeline.
demand_pricing: Approval rates dipped by about 3-4% because of the Fusion+2 guardrail imposed during the West Asia crisis; guardrail now lifted in category A branches (about 80% of branches) and retained in lower-category branches.
Collection efficiency stayed above 99.7% through July and early August across the large states, including rain-fed and heat-affected states.

Recovery: external agencies handled about 30% of hard-bucket recoveries until last quarter, now moved in-house with AI partners; INR35 crore per quarter from 60+ DPD book and INR21 crore from written-off accounts in Q1.
Write-off recovery opportunity estimated at about INR600 crore; at about 30% settlement, about INR180 crore over 15-18 months, against an average of about INR7 crore per month currently.
Management argues competition is thinning because scarce capital is concentrated among a few players and the subprime segment has exited formal MFI.

qa_highlights.question: Will management overlay be released again and what was the Q1 position?
qa_highlights.answer: No management overlay was released in Q1; the INR10 crore release was in Q4 FY26. Overlay balance is INR19.5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will MFI deliver the heavy lifting of growth given lower approval rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Fusion+2 guardrail lifted in about 80% of branches; about 45% of H1 disbursement needed for INR10,000 crore AUM is expected from existing channels, with individual loans only contributing from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR14 crore finance cost impact and does it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: MTM impact was INR3.93 crore and will not recur; net impact of excess liquidity about INR3.5-4 crore; management said it will drop out once liquidity is normalised, so the delta is about INR8 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the excess liquidity drag last?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing was under INR50 crore in July; liquidity is to fall from INR1,880 crore to about INR1,400-1,450 crore by end Q2, in line with internal policy of a few months' disbursement cover.

qa_highlights.question: Where will NIM settle over the next few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 15-20 bps further NIM expansion by year-end, assuming no rate cuts; 55 bps yield hikes, of which 12 bps is in the book now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 opex about INR830 crore; Q1 FY27 about INR204-205 crore. AOP assumes 4-5% growth, with 2-3% saving targeted; long-term opex to average AUM about 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: When will capital be raised and what is the trigger?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital adequacy 36.95% and leverage 2.32x; capital sufficient for about 2 years. Board-level roadshows about 6-7 months before need, around mid-FY28; internal floor of 23-25% Tier 1 versus 15% regulatory.

risks_watch: Rate cuts would offset the NIM expansion path; management says a minor rate increase has little impact.
Monsoon, El Nino and West Asia conflict effects on rain-fed states; the company says collection efficiency has held so far.
ECL coverage ratios fell at face value due to portfolio mix shift (Stage 2 and 3 share down, MSME secured), not because of lower provisioning in each segment; to monitor.
Execution risk on the individual loan launch, MSME scale-up from about INR50 crore a month, and new-customer acquisition under the relaxed guardrail.
Sharp AUM growth of about 4% QoQ needs to accelerate substantially in H2 to reach the INR10,000 crore FY27 target, with approval rates under pressure.
Unrecognised DTA of INR290 crore means PAT stays below PBT for about two years as it is utilised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and margins, with specific numbers offered on most questions. Less specific on the AUM target path, where management pointed to H1 disbursement shares and early-August run rates rather than hard data. Evasive when asked about the Tier 1 trigger and on whether GNPA continues to fall, which was deferred to trend commentary.
key_quotes: The customer who remains is, in our view, better placed to service our obligations and navigate the external headwinds than she was at the start of the previous cycle.
FY26 was about rebuilding Fusion. FY27 is about showing what the rebuilt Fusion can deliver.
The first phase of our earning recovery was driven largely by normalizing credit costs. The next phase should increasingly be driven by average AUM growth and operating leverage.

adds.what: Net branch reduction of about 40-50 (50-60 openings, about 100 closures) by Q3 FY27; branch network capped around 1,350-1,400
Individual loan product launch (avg ticket ~INR1.5 lakh), expected ~10% of MFI disbursements over time
MSME scale-up using ~200 MFI branches as hub-and-spoke (~50 taken up now), entering Tamil Nadu; MSME to 15% of mix next year, 20% in two years

growth.why: Management retains the INR10,000 crore FY27 AUM target (from INR7,702 crore, implying ~30% growth in the remaining year, with 44-45% of disbursements in H1 and 55% in H2) and frames 20-25% CAGR longer term; delivery rests on disbursements up 88% YoY, guardrail relaxation in ~80% of category A branches, an individual loan launch in early September and MSME scale-up, with no hard capacity additions

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 11.93% (+49 bps QoQ, +160 bps YoY) with management guiding a further 15-20 bps (up to 25 bps) by year-end assuming no rate cuts, and only 12 bps of 55 bps customer yield hikes reflected so far; marginal cost of borrowing fell to 10.1% from 12.6%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Net branch count falls by about 40-50 (about 100 closures vs 50-60 openings) with the network capped at about 1,350-1,400; no new plants or capacity additions, and the only addition is the individual loan product and MSME hub-and-spoke using existing branches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM of INR7,702 crore must reach INR10,000 crore by FY27 end (~30% growth in the rest of the year, 55% of disbursements in H2) versus only ~4% QoQ growth now; disbursements +88% YoY and guardrail relaxed in ~80% of category A branches support it, but the run rate is not yet there.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the company is shrinking its branch footprint and capital is sufficient for about 2 years at 36.95% CAR, with the next raise around mid-FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management points to NIM up to 25 bps more and credit cost nearer 2% than the 2.5% guide, but AUM growth must accelerate sharply before any revenue guide raise is credible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: AUM target needs roughly 30% growth in the remaining year against ~4% QoQ now, with approval rates down 3-4% and individual loans only contributing from Q3; rate cuts would also offset the NIM path.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Individual loan product Board-approved with system work underway and first loan targeted by first week of September 2026 at ~INR1.5 lakh average ticket, expected to reach ~10% of MFI disbursements over time.

rows.label: MSME scale-up with hub-and-spoke into Tamil Nadu
rows.why: MSME book about INR800 crore disbursing about INR50 crore a month; target 15% of mix next year and 20% in two years, using about 50 of 200 identified MFI branches now.

rows.label: Write-off recovery upside
rows.why: Write-off recovery opportunity of about INR600 crore; at about 30% settlement that is about INR180 crore versus about INR7 crore per month currently, though this is management's estimate.

rows.label: Liquidity drawdown to INR1,400-1,450 crore
rows.why: Balance-sheet liquidity of INR1,880 crore is targeted to fall by end Q2, removing the excess-liquidity drag of about INR3.5-4 crore and lifting cost-of-funds efficiency.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, NIM path and cost of funds, with specific numbers on most questions; it was cautious and evasive on the AUM target path and the Tier 1 capital trigger, deferring GNPA direction to trend commentary.
